text:
maria: FYI customer C-129 reporting big p95/p99 spikes on the /generate-with-tools endpoint after they enabled structured output validation. Started ~2026-03-10 14:02 UTC. collecting details now.

aj: Can you paste the exact error/latency numbers? and which model+plan?

maria: They said p95 went from ~120ms to ~800ms, p99 ~1.5s. Happens on live traffic (dedicated). Model: rdx-large-1, runtime: dedicated-gpu-pool-3. Enabled JSON schema validation + tool router.

devon: Any correlation with CPU or qps?

maria: Observability shows CPU on the api-router node jumping to ~90% during incidents. QPS steady. Traces show long time inside "validateStructuredOutput" and "toolRouter.route()" spans.

observability-bot: Alert: increased p99 duration on route=generate-with-tools (service=api-router) from 120ms to 1.4s at 2026-03-10T14:02:31Z. Top traces: 60% validation, 30% router serial dispatch.

aj: Okay likely two things: expensive JSON schema validation (compiled validators not reused?) and tool router doing synchronous sequential tool calls (no parallelism). Repro steps?

maria: Customer provided a small repro payload. Posting simplified curl:

```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{
  "model": "rdx-large-1",
  "structured_output": {
    "schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"answer":{"type":"string"}},"required":["answer"]},
    "validate": true
  },
  "tools": ["wiki-lookup","code-runner"],
  "input": "Summarize..."
}'
```

maria: With ~100 concurrent clients reproduces p99 regression locally.

kevin: Do we precompile validators (ajv) per-schema? My memory: we cache compiled validators keyed by schema digest, but cache TTL might be misconfigured. If customers send slightly different schemas each request (e.g., timestamps, doc ids) then cache misses blow up CPU.

sophia: Also router: it loops tools sequentially and executes each tool via a sync HTTP call to tool-proxy from the same api-router process. If validation waits until after all tool calls to validate the final json, we might be blocking CPU+IO on the same thread.

devon: Can we see a flamegraph?

maria: Attached trace snippet (transcribed):
```
span: api-router.handleRequest 0-1400ms
  span: toolRouter.route 0-1100ms
    span: toolProxy.call(wiki-lookup) 0-300ms
    span: toolProxy.call(code-runner) 300-900ms
  span: validateStructuredOutput 1100-1380ms
```

aj: That ordering is interesting — router finished tool calls, then validation. But observability earlier said validate took 60% — maybe both per-tool mini-validations + final validation? Could be multiple validations: per-tool output schema + final top-level schema.

maria: Customer confirmed they enable per-tool validation AND final schema validation. So multiple expensive steps.

kevin: Quick mitigations: 1) re-enable compiled validator cache, increase cache size and make keying tolerant (strip non-schema params). 2) Precompile common schemas at startup. 3) For dedicated customers, offer an opt-in background validation mode: return response immediately and validate asynchronously, marking as "validation_pending" in metadata. 4) Limit per-request tool router concurrency and move tool calls to a worker pool so api-router CPU isn't blocked. 5) Provide a per-route toggle to disable validation until we fully fix.

aj: For immediate customer relief, disable structured validation for that customer. We can flip a feature flag on the dedicated control plane. Maria do you want me to do the toggle?

maria: Yes please. Customer agreed to temporary disable.

aj: Doing toggle now...

deploy-bot: rollout:feature-toggle update customer=C-129 feature=structured_validation state=off scope=route:/generate-with-tools started by=aj

deploy-bot: rollout:feature-toggle update customer=C-129 feature=structured_validation state=off - success (propagated to dedicated-gpu-pool-3)

maria: Customer reported immediate improvement: p95 back to ~150ms, p99 ~220ms. :thumbsup:

sophia: Good. Next steps to fix platform-wide: open infra ticket to harden validator caching and to refactor router to avoid in-process blocking. I'll own the router-side refactor.

aj: I'll open two tickets: validator cache (#4782) and async-validation/flagging (#4783). Assigning to kevin and aj respectively.

kevin: I'll also add a metric for validator cache hit rate and an alert if hit rate < 80% for 5m.

devon: For a medium-term improvement: precompile validators into WASM or use an embedded engine that runs faster (we tried ajv with precompile earlier). Also consider batching validation for identical schemas across concurrent requests.

maria: Customer wants ETA for permanent fix. We gave temporary fix and noted planned work. They asked for a timeline.

aj: For the customer SLA answer: we can say short-term fix done (feature toggle), medium-term (validator cache tuning + alerts) ~2 weeks, router refactor and async validation ~6-8 weeks depending on scope. I'll sync with eng on priorities.

sophia: I'll draft a short changelog and design doc for the router refactor. Will link here when ready.

observability-bot: Note: manual annotation - incident resolved for customer C-129 at 2026-03-10T14:12:50Z after feature toggle.

maria: Adding repro notes to the support ticket with the curl above and the trace snippet.

support-bot: Ticket update: C-129 - temporary disable of structured validation applied. Next: engineering fixes tracked in #4782 #4783.

aj: Any objections to making the validation toggle available as a per-tenant default in Dedicated UI? would help customers self-serve.

kevin: +1. but we should hide behind a warning and require consent since it's a quality tradeoff.

devon: Also add an example in the docs about how structured validation impacts latency and how to design schemas for performance: small, reuse, avoid regex-heavy rules.

maria: Great. I'll follow up with the customer tomorrow with the timeline and link to the ticket. Thanks all. :heart:

kevin: Filing perf postmortem after root-cause analysis. Assigning to eng-runtime.

aj: Closing thread after PRs and alerts are in place.

maria: Thread closed.
